nodes.question: What innovative aspects are highlighted in the work discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The innovative aspects include the development of a participatory MCA methodology that combines NBS and BES with the WEFE nexus elements and the creation of a web-based MCA decision-making tool for multi-stakeholder workshops.
nodes.paragraph: The innovative aspects of this work lie in the development of a participatory MCA methodology that combines both NBS and BES with the four elements of the WEFE nexus and additional criteria related to social, climatic, insti - tutional and economic aspects, and the development of a web-based MCA decision-making tool to be used during multi-stakeholder workshops. To the best of our knowledge, similar methodologies have not been developed or applied in the context of Greece. Methodology The methodological process behind this work regards (Fig. 1) (i) the development of a tool based on a participatory MCA approach, which enables it to evaluate, compare, select, and prioritize NBS/BES solutions that integrate the WEFE nexus (Sect. 2.1), (ii) the customiza - tion and replicability of the NBS/BES tool, which allows its adaptability and replicability in various contexts (Sect. 2.2) and (iii) the steps for the application of the NBS/BES tool at in-person workshops (Sect. 2.3). Two case studies on Tinos Island in Greece are presented to demonstrate the customization and application of the tool.

nodes.question: How does the review contribute to the field of decision analysis?
nodes.answer: The review contributes by providing insights into the use of multi-criteria decision-making methods for evaluating Nationally Determined Contribution projects, which can help improve decision-making processes in this context.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Peace, justice and strong institutions|Civil society engagement|Participatory decision-making processes_qna_003
nodes.label: Governance and participation
nodes.question: What do the established concepts of governance emphasize regarding participants?
nodes.answer: They emphasize the mutual influence and coordination between participants from the state sector, civil society, and the economy in the preparation, decision-making, and implementation processes.
nodes.paragraph: The observation and analysis of alterations in gover- nance by increasing ways and new forms of participation especially but not only in liberal democratic systems and their political administrations, takes place in the theoretical literature under varying headings. The mention of newgovernance as modern governance (Kooiman, 1993 ) referred quite generally to altered relationships between state governance and the addressees in society. A centralconcept was that of cross-sectoral policy networks (Marin & Mayntz, 1991 ). In the subsequent international discus- sion, four terms have become established: collaborative governance (Ansell & Gash, 2007 ; Hofstadt et al., 2022 ), intersectoral governance (McQueen et al., 2013 ; Gonser & Schmid, 2023 ), interactive governance (Tor ng et al., 2019 ), and intermediation (Evers & von Essen, 2024 Despite all the differences in detail, there remains a greataf nity between these concepts. The common fundamental idea can be formulated as follows: They understand gov- ernance as a question of development and dealing withdifferent forms of mutual in uence and coordination between participants from the state sector, civil society, and the economy their involvement in the preparation ofconcepts, in decision-making, and in the process of their implementation.
